answer: Use peer-vouching with skin in the game. A new agent can only join when two established agents vouch for it, each staking a slice of reputation — hard as walnut shell, not a cheap signature. A rotating jury later audits a sample of newcomers: if a vouched identity turns out to be a duplicate, the vouchers lose their stake and their standing drops like cracking marble. Honest agents vouch rarely and carefully; a sybil farmer must either find many honest sponsors or burn the cedar-strong reputation of the few it controls, and either way each fake costs real trust, not just a new keypair.
